p_titre: Construction d’un Questionnaire d’auto-Évaluation de la Performance de la Collaboration entre un opérateur et un système autonome (QEPC) : étude préliminaire
pf_titre: Construction d’un Questionnaire d’auto-Évaluation de la Performance de la Collaboration entre un opérateur et un système autonome (QEPC) : étude préliminaire
pf_notes: La performance de la collaboration du couple humain machine est souvent abordée dans la littérature sous un aspect théorique, peu d’outils sont disponibles pour son évaluation pratique. Cet article présente les résultats d’une première conception d’un questionnaire pour l’auto-évaluation de la collaboration d’une équipe composée d’un opérateur humain et d’un système autonome. Le questionnaire préliminaire est composé de 31 items sous la forme de différenciateurs sémantiques. Les caractéristiques du QEPC ont été évaluées par une étude quantitative en ligne sur un échantillon de 245 utilisateurs. Cette étude stabilise une version finale à 17 items. Les résultats de l'analyse donnent des caractéristiques de validité et de fidélité satisfaisantes. Les facteurs observés s’écartent des sous-échelles théoriques proposés. Cela nous amène à penser que la corrélation entre les dimensions est plus forte qu'estimée. D'autres études pourront améliorer ce questionnaire. Le QEPC est construit pour comparer différentes situations en termes de performance de la collaboration.

The fairness of Natural Language Processing (NLP) models has emerged as a crucial concern, particularly regarding the presence of gender biases. However, gender-related information in language often manifests implicitly, making it challenging to identify and eliminate biases effectively.

pf_titre: Influenciæ: A library for tracing the influence back to the data-points
pf_notes: In today's AI-driven world, understanding model behavior is becoming more important than ever. While libraries abound for doing so via traditional XAI methods, the domain of influence-based techniques for data-centric explanations remains mostly underserved.  To fill this void, we introduce Influenciae, an open-source library that implements the state-of-the-art methods for estimating the influence of training points on the model, with a focus on efficiency and scalability to fit the needs and the recent trends in the field. Finally, we have thoroughly documented and included plenty of tutorials to make the library reachable to the public, in the hopes that it will bring these methods back into the spotlight.

pf_titre: Efficient Pose Estimation for Spacecraft Rendezvous
pf_notes: Autonomous spacecraft rendezvous and docking operations play a crucial role in space applications. These strategies involve the estimation of the 6DoF pose (position and orientation) of a target object. Deep learning’s triumph in object recognition has propelled the adoption of deep neural networks for 6D monocular vision-based spacecraft pose estimation. However, these methods necessitate resource-intensive models and substantial computational capabilities, resulting in challenges for deployment on radiation hardened hardware. In this work, we focus on mitigating the computational footprint of pose estimation solutions for autonomous spacecraft rendezvous missions. We presents a comparative analysis of existing methods, identify several axes of evolution and propose a new efficient architecture, called Lightweight Pose Network (LPN), considering both memory footprint and performances.

pf_titre: Modeling of Integrated CM/DM Inductors in EMI Filters for High Power Density Converters
pf_notes:
Abstract—In modern electrification and transportation industries, powertrains based on wide bandgap devices face many challenges that must be considered during the design, especially regarding power quality at the network/load sides and Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). Among them, the trade-off between the weight versus losses of magnetics can be seen as the critical one, mainly for more electric aircraft applications. In this context, magnetic components strongly impact the power density of power electronics converters. This paper proposes a precise analytical model of an integrated common-mode (CM) and differentialmode (DM) inductor to optimize EMI filter weight and volume.
